TABLE.NAME: local_reportlms_userstate
TABLE.COMMENT: Which learners changed since their data was last accepted by Report LMS.

FIELD.NAME: dirty
FIELD.COMMENT: 1 when this learner has changes not yet confirmed by the SaaS. This is what the push selects on.

FIELD.NAME: timechanged
FIELD.COMMENT: When a change was last noticed.

FIELD.NAME: timepushed
FIELD.COMMENT: When the SaaS last confirmed this learner.

FIELD.NAME: contenthash
FIELD.COMMENT: Hash of the slice last accepted, so an unchanged learner is skipped instead of re-sent.

INDEX.NAME: dirty
INDEX.COMMENT: The push reads WHERE dirty = 1, so this is the index that keeps it cheap at 100k learners.

TABLE.NAME: local_reportlms_node
TABLE.COMMENT: Organisation units somebody typed in, rather than derived from a profile field.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: What people call it. Hashed on the way out like any profile-field value, so this never leaves the site.

FIELD.NAME: parentid
FIELD.COMMENT: The sector above it, or null for a top-level unit.

FIELD.NAME: kind
FIELD.COMMENT: sector or department, matching the wire contract.

TABLE.NAME: local_reportlms_member
TABLE.COMMENT: Who is in which unit. One row per learner per node.

FIELD.NAME: source
FIELD.COMMENT: manual or auto. The column the whole design rests on: it is what lets a push rebuild derived membership every run without touching a row somebody typed.

INDEX.NAME: useridsource
INDEX.COMMENT: A learner is looked up by id to find out whether a manual row claims them before auto-detect places them.

TABLE.NAME: local_reportlms_manager
TABLE.COMMENT: Who manages a unit. Names either a user or a role, never both.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: One person. Null when this row names a role instead.

FIELD.NAME: roleid
FIELD.COMMENT: Everyone holding this role manages the unit, which is how a site with staff turnover avoids editing this table every time somebody joins.

TABLE.NAME: local_reportlms_source
TABLE.COMMENT: What a unit draws its people from. Resolved at read time, never stored as membership.

FIELD.NAME: itemtype
FIELD.COMMENT: course, category, group, cohort or profilefield. Also the specificity order: a group is narrower than the course holding it.

FIELD.NAME: itemid
FIELD.COMMENT: course.id, course_categories.id, groups.id, cohort.id, or user_info_field.id for a profile value.

FIELD.NAME: itemvalue
FIELD.COMMENT: The profile value for itemtype=profilefield, empty for the rest. Empty rather than null so the unique index treats two of them as the same row. No column default: every writer states the value, and XMLDB rejects an empty string as a default.

INDEX.NAME: nodeitem
INDEX.COMMENT: One unit draws from one thing once. Saying it twice is not saying it more firmly.

INDEX.NAME: item
INDEX.COMMENT: Answers which units draw from this course, which is what anything reacting to an enrolment needs.
